sentences.text: ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Shubash Chand S/o Jaymal, Village Dobi Ward No. 4  Tehsil Bhadra Dist. Hanumangarh
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Kuldeep Sharma
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sameer Pareek, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI CHIRANIA Order 06/11/2025 1.

The instant bail application under Section 483 B.N.S.S. (439 Cr. P.C.) has been filed by accused-applicant Satveer, who is in custody in connection with FIR No.254/2023 registered at P.S.
Bhadra, District Hanumangarh for offence under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(N) IPC and Section 5L/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, against rejection order dated 02.8.2025 passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Court No.1, Hanumangarh in Criminal Misc. Case No.208/2025 (Sessions Case No.125/2023).
2. Earlier bail applications filed by the petitioner were rejected by this Court vide orders dated 29.1.2024 & 17.12.2024.

sentences.text: Thereafter, on account of change in circumstance and subsequent events taken place i.e. statement of prosecutrix has been recorded, hence, this third bail.
3. Learned counsel submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case.

As a matter of fact, the complainant-girl, who is a student of first year graduation, developed friendliness with Satveer vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:47625) on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169704993/
1 present petitioner.
She of her own sweet will left her house alongwith petitioner.

They travelled together by various public transports and stayed at different cities where family members of petitioner's side were living and at no point of time she ever raised any hue or cry as regards her alleged abduction.
The petitioner has not committed any offence, as alleged.

The prosecutrix was a consenting party as she wanted to perform marriage with petitioner, thus, keeping in view long incarceration period i.e. since 15.7.2023, and the fact that the trial of case will sufficiently take a long time in its conclusion, a prayer was made to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
4. Learned PP strongly opposed the application stating that there are no contradiction and inconsistency in the statements of prosecutrix.
The allegations against the petitioner, being of serious nature, his conduct disentitles him of any relief from this Court.

5. This Court has gone through the complete charge-sheet; statement of prosecutrix recorded by trial court, as PW-2, under Section 164 Cr. P.C., dated 23.7.2024, which sufficiently goes to show that the prosecutrix herself wanted to perform marriage with the petitioner and with that intent she left her house and joined (Uploaded on 06/11/2025 at 06:00:36 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:47625] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-10935/2025] petitioner's company.
She entered into consensual relationship with the petitioner.
They stayed together in different cities in the house of family members of petitioner's side.

There being major contradictions and inconsistencies in the statements of the prosecutrix and prima facie the allegation appears to be not true, thus, considering the long incarceration period,
this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

6. Consequently, this bail application filed under Section 483 B.N.S.S. is allowed and it is directed that petitioner Satveer S/o.Rameshwar Lal shall be released on bail in connection with FIR No.254/2023 registered at P.S. Bhadra, District Hanumangarh provided he execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sound and solvent sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of learned trial court for his appearance before that court on each and every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till the completion of the trial.

(RAVI CHIRANIA),J 105-Sanjay/-
